source.title: Atlas-Alignment: Making Interpretability Transferable Across Language Models
source.authors: Bruno Puri; Jim Berend; S. Lapuschkin; W. Samek

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates cross-model latent-space alignment and transfer using its own semantic-retention, feature-retrieval, and steering measures. It does not reproduce the original Platonic Representation Hypothesis measurement.
record.gate_note: The paper tests whether shared-input linear alignments transfer semantic structure across language models, and how outcomes vary with alignment method, pooling, and training-set size. Cited claims about the Platonic Representation Hypothesis are background, not results. The evaluated models all process text; the study does not test convergence with model capability or cross-modal image-caption alignment.
record.test_reason: The study fits linear maps on shared text inputs from eight language models (GPT-2, Qwen 2.5 0.5B/1.5B/3B, Ministral-8B, three Llama-3.1-8B variants) into a Gemma-2-2B SAE latent space. It measures how much semantic structure survives: AP/AUROC ranking preservation, feature-retrieval MRR/MPP and steering faithfulness against random and native baselines. That bears directly on V4, mappability with little loss by a simple linear map. Comparing alignment methods, pooling and fit-set size shows how strongly measured transfer depends on these choices (V6). It is framed as an interpretability method, but its outcome measures are cross-model mappability, so it is not only T4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that lightweight linear alignment, especially Orthogonal Procrustes, to a labeled SAE Concept Atlas gives robust semantic transfer, reliable concept retrieval and controllable steering across model families. They argue this amortizes interpretability cost. They also say alignment method and pooling choice matter, and that when and how widely the Platonic and Linear Representation Hypotheses hold remains open.
record.recipe_differences: Uses shared text inputs and linear latent-space mappings to transfer an atlas's semantics, then evaluates translation quality, feature retrieval, and steering; it does not reproduce the original Platonic Representation Hypothesis method.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment method changes retrieval and translation outcomes; mean versus max pooling changes alignment quality; alignment-training sample size changes translation quality.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the results. The study uses a Gemma 2 2B-derived atlas, selected model layers, and shared text inputs; it does not establish performance-related convergence or test other modalities. Retrieval is evaluated on 454 filtered features, and its alignment-quality test averages over 100 randomly selected atlas features.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit was reached. Omitted additional metrics and method/model combinations in Tables 1, 5, and 7; the training-size MRR results in Table 8; steering activation-change values and alternative methods in Table 3; and native-steering comparisons in Table 10. The retained rows prioritize separate model/layer AP results, retrieval methods and atlases, training-size and pooling conditions, and Procrustes steering outcomes. r60 is an accidental duplicate of r59 and should be disregarded.

untested.parts: Stitching layers, relative representations and mapping without paired data. All maps target one SAE atlas (Gemma 2 2B, layer 20), not raw model-to-model spaces or arbitrary model pairs.
Out-of-distribution inputs, the number-of-neighbours settings of kNN-style metrics, and standard similarity measures such as CKA or mutual kNN. Only map type, pooling and fit-set size vary.
No test of alignment versus capability. Qwen 0.5B/1.5B/3B AP 0.39/0.41/0.42 is not analysed as a scale trend, and the authors note inter-model spread is similar to layer spread.
No test of whether the same features recur across models.
No test of plateau with scale or of shared data or objectives as the cause.

missing.what: Native vs translated steering. Procrustes f 19.62/38.40/36.67/28.41/37.82 vs native 16.85/48.61/51.10/34.13/38.31 at Llama-IT layers 3/12/19/25/30; average gap 5.6 points. This is direct evidence on 'little loss' for V4.

Retrieval vs fit-set size. Linear regression MRR is 0.85 at 10k but collapses to 0.03 at 500k, while Procrustes rises from 0.36 to 0.97. This is strong evidence that measured transfer depends on method and data jointly.
Pooling effect reverses by method. Covariance, cross-correlation and Semantic Lens AP rise under mean pooling (e.g. Semantic Lens Qwen 3B 0.16→0.26), while Procrustes and OLS fall.
Steering faithfulness for non-Procrustes methods across layers. Covariance f ranges from 3.50 to 39.76 and is unstable across models and layers.

record.verdict_notes: All subject models are mapped into a single atlas: Gemma 2 2B residual stream at layer 20 via Gemma Scope SAEs, with shared Pile text as inputs. 'Interchangeability' is therefore always into an SAE basis, never model to model in raw space. Rows r01–r20 fix max pooling and the MLP layer. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The slight AP rise across Qwen sizes (r02–r04) is not analysed by the authors and is too small to bear on V1. The study is not an original source for any version.

versions.untested_parts: The study includes differently sized Qwen models but does not test whether alignment rises with capability or performance, and does not measure performance as a function of scale.
No vision-language or paired image-caption alignment is tested.
No comparisons across random initializations of the same architecture are reported.

Tests shared-input linear translation, especially Orthogonal Procrustes, between language-model latent spaces and a Concept Atlas. It does not test stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired/shared inputs.
The study retrieves subject-model features associated with atlas concepts, but does not test whether the same interpretable features or circuits recur across models.
Tests sensitivity to alignment method, activation pooling, and amount of alignment-training data. It does not test out-of-distribution inputs or the number-of-neighbours settings named in the claim.
Does not test whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment, or whether alignment plateaus as a function of model scale.

relationships.condition: Orthogonal Procrustes map, Llama-IT L19 retrieval and steering in GPT-2, Qwen 3B and Llama-IT
relationships.reason: Retrieval is near perfect (MRR 0.97, MPP 0.92–0.94; r41–r44). Translated directions steer far above random (f 24–85 vs ~1.5; r57–r59). Per the text (Table 10, not in rows), Procrustes trails native steering by only 5.6 f points on average.
relationships.display_finding: Retrieval reached MRR 0.97 and MPP 0.92–0.94, while translated steering achieved f values of 24–85 versus about 1.5 for random directions and averaged 5.6 points below native steering.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Orthogonal Procrustes map, Llama-IT L19 retrieval and steering in GPT-2, Qwen 3B and Llama-IT
source_check.reason: Table 2 confirms r41–r44: MRR 0.97 and MPP 0.92–0.94. Table 3 confirms r57–r59 exceed random steering. Appendix A.8 additionally reports a 5.6-point average faithfulness gap to native steering for Llama-IT.

relationships.condition: Ranking-preservation test across all subject models and layers under Procrustes
relationships.reason: AP is 0.36–0.49 vs random 0.046 across models and layers. That is well above chance but far from lossless preservation of feature–sample rankings (r01–r20).
relationships.display_finding: Procrustes achieved average precision 0.36–0.49 versus random 0.046, exceeding chance but preserving feature–sample rankings incompletely.

source_check.condition: Ranking-preservation test across all subject models and layers under Procrustes
source_check.reason: Table 5 confirms AP 0.36–0.49 versus random 0.046, including r01–r12: substantial but incomplete preservation of feature–sample relationships.

relationships.condition: Other simple linear maps (OLS, covariance, cross-correlation) and small fit sets
relationships.reason: Unconstrained linear regression retrieval is near random (MRR 0.02–0.03; r33–r36). Covariance and cross-correlation give MRR 0.12–0.26 (r25–r32). Procrustes with 1k samples gives AP 0.21 (r45). Low loss holds only for the orthogonal map with enough data.
relationships.display_finding: In the tested fitting regime, OLS retrieval was near random at MRR 0.02–0.03, covariance and cross-correlation achieved 0.12–0.26, and Procrustes with 1,000 samples achieved average precision 0.21.
